checks: Primary reactance at 1.80 MHz: 346 Ω = 6.9× 50 Ω (L = 26.88 µH, 21.50–32.25 µH with AL tolerance).
Mix 43 is lossy at 54.0 MHz (µ'' 145 > µ' 59); expect extra loss at the top end.

Average core loss 9.83 W (9.83 W key-down at 5.33 MHz × 100% duty) = 431 mW/cm³ (Fair-Rite: ≤300 conservative, ≤500 max).

Conductor current up to 2.12 A RMS = 1.6 A/mm² (limit 5).
10 conductor passes; about 52 fit in one layer around the 35.55 mm hole → 1 layer(s), 3% of the hole area.
High-impedance side ≈ 212 V RMS (300 V peak) at worst-case SWR.
Ruthroff: wind the wires as a tight, evenly twisted bundle. The core carries the full signal flux, so it runs warmer than a Guanella (ham.stackexchange 9:1 notes; G3TXQ unun experiments).
Above 30 MHz (6 m) most ferrite transformers lose efficiency and match quality; check 6 m on the analyser or use a separate 6 m antenna.

checks: Primary reactance at 1.80 MHz: 259 Ω = 5.2× 50 Ω (L = 32.91 µH, 26.33–39.49 µH with AL tolerance).
Mix 31 is lossy at 54.0 MHz (µ'' 148 > µ' 59); expect extra loss at the top end.
Peak flux (saturation, PEP, SWR 3:1) 21.0 mT = 5.8% of 360 mT at 1.80 MHz.
Flux above the Amidon/DL5SWB heating guideline (~150/√f G) at 1.80 MHz (140 G > 112 G), 1.90 MHz (133 G > 109 G), 2.00 MHz (126 G > 106 G).
Average core loss 20.00 W (20 W key-down at 1.90 MHz × 100% duty) = 877 mW/cm³ (Fair-Rite: ≤300 conservative, ≤500 max).
Estimated temperature rise 103 °C → core about 133 °C at 30 °C ambient (Curie 130 °C; Amidon: keep ≤75 °C continuous, ≤100 °C intermittent).

Core (magnetizing) efficiency into a matched load ≈ 91.1% (0.40 dB) at 1.90 MHz, the worst evaluated frequency; 80.0% with the voltage raised by SWR 3:1. For scale: DG1JAN measured ~76–78% total for an FT240-43 2:15 EFHW (this model gives ~74% for 2 turns at 7 MHz).
Conductor current up to 2.12 A RMS = 1.6 A/mm² (limit 5).
12 conductor passes; about 52 fit in one layer around the 35.55 mm hole → 1 layer(s), 4% of the hole area.
High-impedance side ≈ 318 V RMS (450 V peak) at worst-case SWR.
Ruthroff: wind the wires as a tight, evenly twisted bundle. The core carries the full signal flux, so it runs warmer than a Guanella (ham.stackexchange 9:1 notes; G3TXQ unun experiments).
Above 30 MHz (6 m) most ferrite transformers lose efficiency and match quality; check 6 m on the analyser or use a separate 6 m antenna.

Autotransformer 1:3: tap section 3 turns (50 Ω side) = 29.02 µH, full winding 9 turns (450 Ω side) = 261.2 µH (L ∝ N², ×9). Rule of thumb: tap-section XL ≥ 4–5 × 50 Ω at the lowest frequency (Cromwell; ARRL handbook practice).

High-frequency limit: unlike the trifilar Ruthroff (a transmission-line transformer), a single tapped winding couples its sections only through the core, so leakage inductance and inter-turn/inter-section capacitance set the upper limit — keep the winding to one layer, spread evenly, and expect SWR to rise on 10–6 m; verify with a 450 Ω test load.

Typical published splits: 3:9 turns on FT140-43 or FT240-43, 4:12 on FT82-43 or stacked FT240-43 (hamradiobase table; Cromwell used 8 tap turns on FT140-43 for extra low-band margin). More turns help 160/80 m but add capacitance that hurts 10–6 m.

Optional compensation capacitor across the SO-239 (as on the 49:1): usually not needed on a 9:1. If SWR into the test load climbs on 10–6 m, try values up to the 49:1 starting value (100 pF, ≥ 1000 V) and keep what flattens the high end.
Above 30 MHz (6 m) most ferrite transformers lose efficiency and match quality; check 6 m on the analyser or use a separate 6 m antenna.
steps: Wind 9 turns of ONE wire in the same direction, spread evenly around the core(s) (not trifilar). Make a tap at turn 3 counted from the start: scrape the insulation/enamel for ~10 mm and solder a short lead, or break the wire there and join both ends to the tap lead.
Start of the winding (turn 0) → SO-239 shell and the ground/counterpoise post.
Tap at turn 3 → SO-239 centre (50 Ω side: turns 0–3, the low-impedance section).
End of the winding (turn 9) → antenna wire terminal (450 Ω side: the full winding).
Check on the analyser with a 450 Ω (e.g. 2 × 910 Ω in parallel, non-inductive) resistor from antenna post to ground post: SWR at the SO-239 should stay below ≈1.5–2:1 across the bands you use.

steps: Wind 21 turns of one wire in the same direction around the core(s). Bunch the first 3 turns tightly; spread the rest evenly (G4AON: first half tight, second half spaced).

End of the winding (turn 21) → antenna wire post. Sleeve the last turns with PTFE.
Compensation capacitor from SO-239 centre to shell (see parts list); tune 47–150 pF on the analyser for best 10–15 m SWR.
Alternative: a separate 3-turn primary twisted over the first turns of the secondary (common in published builds).

Scrape the enamel and tap at turn 44 → SO-239 centre pin (the 50 Ω input).
End of the winding (turn 308) → antenna wire post. Sleeve the last turns with PTFE.
Compensation capacitor from SO-239 centre to shell (see parts list); tune 47–150 pF on the analyser for best 10–15 m SWR.
Alternative: a separate 44-turn primary twisted over the first turns of the secondary (common in published builds).

checks: Primary reactance at 1.80 MHz: 254 Ω = 5.1× 50 Ω (L = 22.46 µH, 21.33–23.58 µH with AL tolerance).

308 conductor passes; about 19 fit in one layer around the 14.48 mm hole → 17 layer(s), 588% of the hole area.

Autotransformer 1:3: tap section 4 turns (50 Ω side) = 34.40 µH, full winding 12 turns (450 Ω side) = 309.6 µH (L ∝ N², ×9). Rule of thumb: tap-section XL ≥ 4–5 × 50 Ω at the lowest frequency (Cromwell; ARRL handbook practice).

High-frequency limit: unlike the trifilar Ruthroff (a transmission-line transformer), a single tapped winding couples its sections only through the core, so leakage inductance and inter-turn/inter-section capacitance set the upper limit — keep the winding to one layer, spread evenly, and expect SWR to rise on 10–6 m; verify with a 450 Ω test load.

Typical published splits: 3:9 turns on FT140-43 or FT240-43, 4:12 on FT82-43 or stacked FT240-43 (hamradiobase table; Cromwell used 8 tap turns on FT140-43 for extra low-band margin). More turns help 160/80 m but add capacitance that hurts 10–6 m.

Optional compensation capacitor across the SO-239 (as on the 49:1): usually not needed on a 9:1. If SWR into the test load climbs on 10–6 m, try values up to the 49:1 starting value (100 pF, ≥ 1000 V) and keep what flattens the high end.

Capacitor 150.5 pF — the coil adds ≈ 1.5 pF self-capacitance, so fit ≈ 149.0 pF, rated ≥ 2000 V (2 × 775 V peak). RF current ≈ 3.65 A RMS (2.00 kVAR). C0G/NP0 HV ceramic disc: Low drift; check the RF-current rating — small discs heat at >1–2 A.

Trap reactance X = 150 Ω. Guidance (ARRL Antenna Book, W8JI): ~100–300 Ω. Higher X → higher Rp (better isolation) but more loading/shortening and loss on the lower band and a narrower bandwidth; lower X → broader, less loading, less isolation.
Unloaded trap Q ≈ 390 (coil 640, capacitor ≈ 1000) → Rp ≈ 58.5 kΩ. W8JI measured 100 kΩ for 100 pF + #12-wire coil at 7 MHz, 250–300 kΩ with copper tubing and vacuum/15 kV caps.
Dissipation on the trap frequency: 5.1 W key-down, 1.5 W average (30% duty) at ≈ 548 V RMS across the trap (√(P·Z_end), Z_end 3000 Ω).
With the coil's self-capacitance in parallel, L with the full 150.5 pF resonates at 7.015 MHz.
steps: Wind 9.16 turns of AWG 12 bare/enamel on a 48.3 mm form (or self-supporting), pitch 4.26 mm, winding length 39.0 mm. Wire: 1551 mm incl. leads.
Mount the 149.0 pF / ≥ 2000 V capacitor directly across the coil ends (shortest leads).
Antenna wire A → one coil end; antenna wire B → the other. Take the wire tension on the form, not on the capacitor.
Tune before installing: grid-dip or analyser with a 1-turn link; squeeze/spread turns to set the resonance slightly below the band (W8JI).
Weatherproof: enclose or coat; moisture lowers Q and shifts resonance.

12 conductor passes; about 52 fit in one layer around the 35.55 mm hole → 1 layer(s), 4% of the hole area.

Autotransformer 1:3: tap section 4 turns (50 Ω side) = 34.40 µH, full winding 12 turns (450 Ω side) = 309.6 µH (L ∝ N², ×9). Rule of thumb: tap-section XL ≥ 4–5 × 50 Ω at the lowest frequency (Cromwell; ARRL handbook practice).

High-frequency limit: unlike the trifilar Ruthroff (a transmission-line transformer), a single tapped winding couples its sections only through the core, so leakage inductance and inter-turn/inter-section capacitance set the upper limit — keep the winding to one layer, spread evenly, and expect SWR to rise on 10–6 m; verify with a 450 Ω test load.

Typical published splits: 3:9 turns on FT140-43 or FT240-43, 4:12 on FT82-43 or stacked FT240-43 (hamradiobase table; Cromwell used 8 tap turns on FT140-43 for extra low-band margin). More turns help 160/80 m but add capacitance that hurts 10–6 m.

Optional compensation capacitor across the SO-239 (as on the 49:1): usually not needed on a 9:1. If SWR into the test load climbs on 10–6 m, try values up to the 49:1 starting value (100 pF, ≥ 1000 V) and keep what flattens the high end.
Above 30 MHz (6 m) most ferrite transformers lose efficiency and match quality; check 6 m on the analyser or use a separate 6 m antenna.

Core (magnetizing) efficiency into a matched load ≈ 96.6% (0.15 dB) at 5.33 MHz, the worst evaluated frequency; 92.3% with the voltage raised by SWR 3:1. For scale: DG1JAN measured ~76–78% total for an FT240-43 2:15 EFHW (this model gives ~74% for 2 turns at 7 MHz).

12 conductor passes; about 52 fit in one layer around the 35.55 mm hole → 1 layer(s), 4% of the hole area.
Antenna terminal ≈ 318 V RMS (450 V peak) at worst-case SWR.

Autotransformer 1:3: tap section 4 turns (50 Ω side) = 34.40 µH, full winding 12 turns (450 Ω side) = 309.6 µH (L ∝ N², ×9). Rule of thumb: tap-section XL ≥ 4–5 × 50 Ω at the lowest frequency (Cromwell; ARRL handbook practice).

High-frequency limit: unlike the trifilar Ruthroff (a transmission-line transformer), a single tapped winding couples its sections only through the core, so leakage inductance and inter-turn/inter-section capacitance set the upper limit — keep the winding to one layer, spread evenly, and expect SWR to rise on 10–6 m; verify with a 450 Ω test load.

Typical published splits: 3:9 turns on FT140-43 or FT240-43, 4:12 on FT82-43 or stacked FT240-43 (hamradiobase table; Cromwell used 8 tap turns on FT140-43 for extra low-band margin). More turns help 160/80 m but add capacitance that hurts 10–6 m.

Optional compensation capacitor across the SO-239 (as on the 49:1): usually not needed on a 9:1. If SWR into the test load climbs on 10–6 m, try values up to the 49:1 starting value (100 pF, ≥ 1000 V) and keep what flattens the high end.
Above 30 MHz (6 m) most ferrite transformers lose efficiency and match quality; check 6 m on the analyser or use a separate 6 m antenna.

checks: Resonance check: L 3.352 µH with C 152.0 pF → 7.050 MHz (VE6YP/K7MEM lumped pF/ft model). XL = XC = 148.5 Ω.

Stub effect: the coax is a transmission-line stub, not a pure capacitor (W8JI measured 164 pF vs 138.5 pF predicted). Expect this winding to resonate near 6.918 MHz (-1.9%). Wind the predicted turns, then spread/compress turns or trim on the analyser — or select the stub-corrected model.
Length/diameter 0.55:1 (K7MEM: 0.4–2, best ≈0.45; W4ULD: 0.25–3, best Q near 0.38).
Bend: form OD 60.3 mm vs coax OD 4.95 mm — keep the form ≥ 10 × coax OD (≥ 49.5 mm) so the centre conductor does not migrate through the dielectric.
Estimated unloaded Q ≈ 237 (Rp ≈ 35.2 kΩ). For scale: W8JI measured Q≈133 (Rp 17.8 kΩ) for an RG-58 7 MHz trap, versus ~465 for a #12-wire L/C trap; W4ULD estimated 215–348 for RG-58 traps.
Trap voltage ≈ 548 V RMS (775 V peak) at 100 W with Z_end ≈ 3000 Ω. Coax dielectric sees up to this between centre and shield; typical rating 1000 V RMS (keep ≤ 50%).

Dissipation if you transmit right on the trap frequency: ≈ 8.5 W key-down, 2.6 W average at 30% duty (ON5VL: RG-58/59 traps tolerate ≈ 35 W). W8JI: never put a trap's resonance inside the band you operate.
Coax stub self-resonance: the 1505 mm of coax is λ/4 near 32.9 MHz — above the trap frequency the trap is capacitive and behaves unpredictably near this frequency.
Inductance cross-check (Nagaoka + Rosa, Coil64 method, shield as round conductor): 3.266 µH vs Wheeler 3.352 µH (-2.6%).
steps: Cut 1555 mm of Custom coax (30.8 pF/ft, VF 0.66, 4.95 mm OD) (1505 mm on the coil incl. 25 mm of pigtails, plus 25 mm each end for terminating).
Drill two holes at each end of the 60.32 mm form, about 48.4 mm apart (winding length 35.7 mm).
Wind 7.21 turns close-wound; pass each end into the form through its holes.
START end: SHIELD → antenna wire A (towards the feed point).
START end: CENTRE conductor → jumper wire run INSIDE the form to the FINISH end, soldered to the SHIELD there (shield-to-centre cross connection).
FINISH end: CENTRE conductor → antenna wire B (outer section).
Before installing: check resonance with a dip meter or an analyser through a 1-turn link (trap not connected); spread or compress turns to tune — aim slightly below the band (W8JI).
Seal both coax ends (silicone or self-amalgamating tape) and keep centre/shield ends apart; strain-relieve the antenna wires on the form, not on the coax.

checks: Air coil: 16.78 turns of Ø0.188 in copper tubing (3/16" nominal) on a 48.3 mm form, pitch 9.53 mm, length 159.8 mm → 4.249 µH (Coil64 helical method; Nagaoka+Rosa 4.180, Wheeler 4.241).
Length/diameter 3.01 (best Q for single-layer coils is around 0.5–1).

Capacitor 120.0 pF (E12 value; exact 112.9 pF) — the coil adds ≈ 2.6 pF self-capacitance; fit the 120.0 pF part and spread the turns slightly to retune, rated ≥ 2000 V (2 × 775 V peak). Trap reactance X = 188 Ω. Guidance (ARRL Antenna Book, W8JI): ~100–300 Ω. Higher X → higher Rp (better isolation) but more loading/shortening and loss on the lower band and a narrower bandwidth; lower X → broader, less loading, less isolation.
Unloaded trap Q ≈ 464 (coil 865, capacitor ≈ 1000) → Rp ≈ 87.3 kΩ. W8JI measured 100 kΩ for 100 pF + #12-wire coil at 7 MHz, 250–300 kΩ with copper tubing and vacuum/15 kV caps.
Dissipation on the trap frequency: 3.4 W key-down, 1.0 W average (30% duty) at ≈ 548 V RMS across the trap (√(P·Z_end), Z_end 3000 Ω).
With the coil's self-capacitance in parallel, L with the full 120.0 pF resonates at 6.974 MHz.
